programme: RORC and NPAS2 form a piece of the core circadian transcriptional loop: RORC transactivates BMAL1 through RORE elements while NPAS2, the CLOCK paralog, heterodimerizes with BMAL1 to drive E-box-controlled output genes. RORC's target set separately carries the Th17/IL-17 immune programme (IL17A, IL17F, IL23R, IFNG, IL6, TNF, FOXP3, CCR6, RORA) and a hepatic xenobiotic-metabolism programme (CYP2C9, CYP2C19), so RORC is the hinge between the clock, immune inflammation, and liver drug/lipid metabolism.
role_in_a: In COPD, RORC's Th17 target module is the documented axis: IL-17-driven neutrophilic/Th17 inflammation and dendritic-cell dysregulation are reported directly for this factor, and disrupted circadian clock output (of which NPAS2-BMAL1 is a core node) tracks with diurnal symptom and exacerbation patterns typical of the disease.
role_in_b: In liver, the same clock loop (RORC/RORE-BMAL1, NPAS2-BMAL1) times hepatocyte proliferation, metabolic zonation, and detoxification (RORC's CYP2C9/CYP2C19 targets sit in this programme); loss of peripheral clock integrity in hepatocytes is an established permissive step toward hepatocellular transformation.
shared_axis: Both organs depend on a peripheral oscillator built from the same RORC/BMAL1/NPAS2 components to gate, respectively, immune tone in the lung and proliferative/metabolic tone in the liver; failure of this shared clock module is a plausible common point of vulnerability even though the two tissues are anatomically and clinically unconnected.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the factors' own targets (RORC->BMAL1, NPAS2-BMAL1 heterodimer, RORC->Th17 genes), and RORC's COPD role is independently placed by three retrieved papers. Nothing in the retrieved record places either factor in liver cancer specifically (no Open Targets association, no on-target PMID), so the liver side of the story rests on the broader circadian-hepatocarcinogenesis literature rather than anything retrieved here - hence supported, not established, and moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 42196213 - three-gene signature and functional validation of immune dysregulation in COPD implicating RORC; PMID 37650285 - circRNA-associated ceRNA network in COPD PBMCs implicating RORC; PMID 38786101 - reduced PD-L1-expressing dendritic cells in COPD associated with RORC-linked pathways. No retrieved PMID places RORC or NPAS2 in liver cancer.
how_to_falsify: ChIP for RORC occupancy at the BMAL1 RORE, and measure BMAL1/PER2 oscillation amplitude, in matched COPD bronchial epithelium versus HCC tumor and adjacent liver; if RORC fails to bind or clock amplitude is intact in one tissue but not the other, the shared-loop claim is wrong. A cleaner test: RORC agonist/antagonist treatment in COPD airway organoids and HCC hepatocyte lines in parallel, scoring IL-17 pathway output in the airway model and CYP2C9/CYP2C19 plus proliferation markers in the liver model - discordant response would falsify a common RORC-driven mechanism.
caveats: Only 2 of the 12 surviving factors (RORC, NPAS2) carry this account; the other 10 (DEAF1, RERE, HNF4G, KDM2B, ZMYND8, FOXP4, HOXA13, BTG2, SMAD5, and discordant YY1) have no coherent placement here and several have very small target sets (<=9 genes), which is a plausible source of network-inference noise rather than shared biology. NPAS2 itself has no Open Targets association with COPD and its retrieved papers concern sleep/cardiac arrhythmia, not COPD or liver cancer - its role in this account is inferred from core-clock biology, not from the record. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 130 patient-group comparisons, so concordance here is not broadly cross-cohort replicated. The tissue pairing (lung vs liver) has no direct anatomical or clinical adjacency, and none of the single-view exclusions (THAP1, SON, ATF6, HOXD11, MYOCD, MAZ, FOXA2, E4F1, NKRF, NR2E1, FOXD2, ZFPM2) are clock- or Th17-related, so this account is not quietly rescuing a factor that failed to generalize.
